dialogue.content: ★こんばんは。本日宜しくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: Good evening. Thank you for your time today.

dialogue.content: こんばんは相談員です。よろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: Good evening, I'm the counselor. It's a pleasure to speak with you.

dialogue.content: ★ネーム教えていただけますか?前回と同じ方なら相談内容を考えようと思って
dialogue.English: Could you please tell me your name? If you’re the same person as last time, I was going to think about what to discuss.

dialogue.content: ドラゴンさんです。
dialogue.English: I'm Dragon.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。承知しました。
dialogue.English: Thank you. I understand.

dialogue.content: ではよろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: Alright then, let's begin.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 最初に年齢と性別を教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: To start, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.content: 50才、女性です
dialogue.English: I'm 50 years old, and female.

dialogue.content: お返事ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing that.

dialogue.content: 今日はどのようなご相談でしょうか？
dialogue.English: What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: 職場の後輩の事なんですが
dialogue.English: It’s about a junior colleague at work.

dialogue.content: はい　後輩さんのどんなことでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see. What about your junior colleague?

dialogue.content: 最近元気がなくて…かなり精神的にまいっているようなんです
dialogue.English: Lately, she seems down... She appears to be quite mentally exhausted.

dialogue.content: それはご心配ですね…
dialogue.English: That must be worrying for you...

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 何か後輩さんが元気がなくなることで、原因のようなものは思い当たるようなことはおありなのですか？
dialogue.English: Do you have any idea what might be causing her to lose her energy?

dialogue.content: 今まで何やかやと相談してくれていたんですが
dialogue.English: She used to come to me for advice about all sorts of things, but...

dialogue.content: ここの所、口数も少なくて
dialogue.English: Lately, she hasn’t been saying much.

dialogue.content: あなたを先輩として頼って来ていたんですね・・・どうしたんでしょうね。
dialogue.English: So she used to rely on you as her senior colleague... I wonder what happened.

dialogue.content: 部署が離れてしまったので、ゆっくり話すこともできなくて、トイレに行く後ろ姿を見ていると、とても心配で、先日声をかけて見たんです。
dialogue.English: Our departments were separated, so we haven't been able to talk properly. Seeing her from behind as she walks to the restroom made me really worried, so I decided to talk to her the other day.

dialogue.content: はい　そうしたら？
dialogue.English: Okay. And then what happened?

dialogue.content: 息子さんの事でした。
dialogue.English: It was about her son.

dialogue.content: おや　ご家族のことでお悩みなっていたんですね・・・
dialogue.English: Oh, so she was worried about a family matter...

dialogue.content: そうなんです。何となく、仕事ではないな、と感じていたんですが・・・反抗期で相当手を焼いているようでした。
dialogue.English: Yes. I had a sense it wasn’t work-related… It seems she’s having quite a hard time with his rebellious phase.

dialogue.content: 息子さんの反抗期・・・なかなか大変そうですね。ちなみに息子さんの学年は？
dialogue.English: Her son’s rebellious phase… that sounds quite challenging. By the way, what grade is he in?

dialogue.content: 中学2年生で、双子の男の子です。
dialogue.English: They’re twin boys in the second year of junior high.

dialogue.content: 一番難しい年頃ですね・・・
dialogue.English: That’s one of the most difficult ages…

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: しかも
dialogue.English: On top of that,

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes?

dialogue.content: 双子で比べられることがずっと続いて来たから、
dialogue.English: Because they're twins, they've constantly been compared to each other,

dialogue.content: なるほど
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: できないお子さんは、ストレスを母親にぶつけるようなんです。
dialogue.English: the one who isn't doing as well seems to take his stress out on his mother.

dialogue.content: お母さんとしては　それをぶつけられると辛いものがありますよね・・・
dialogue.English: As a mother, having that directed at her must be very painful...

dialogue.content: そうですね。
dialogue.English: Yes, it is.

dialogue.content: 生まれる時も
dialogue.English: Even when they were born,

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes?

dialogue.content: なかなか妊娠しなくて
dialogue.English: she had trouble conceiving,

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 体外受精で生まれたんです
dialogue.English: and they were born through IVF.

dialogue.content: 旦那さんとは別居状態で
dialogue.English: She's separated from her husband,

dialogue.content: 働きながら、塾の送り迎えをして
dialogue.English: and while working, she drives them to and from cram school,

dialogue.content: それは大変そう。
dialogue.English: That sounds very tough.

dialogue.content: 近所でも評判の私学に合格させたんです
dialogue.English: She managed to get them into a well-regarded private school in the neighborhood.

dialogue.content: すごいですね。
dialogue.English: That's amazing.

dialogue.content: 彼女にとっては、手塩にかけた自慢の息子なのに
dialogue.English: For her, they are her pride and joy, sons she's painstakingly raised, and yet,

dialogue.content: 反抗されて泣いてしまったら、
dialogue.English: when she cried because of his rebellious behavior,

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes?

dialogue.content: 生まなきゃ良かったんだろうって言われたそうです
dialogue.English: he apparently told her, 'You probably wish you hadn't given birth to me.'

dialogue.content: そんなこと言われたら、あんまりですよ・・・
dialogue.English: To be told something like that... that's just too cruel.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。独身の頃から彼女を知っているだけに、何とかしてあげたくて
dialogue.English: I agree. I’ve known her since before she was married, so I really want to help her somehow.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。あなたとしては、どんなことを言ってあげているのですか？
dialogue.English: I can understand that. What have you been saying to her?

dialogue.content: 初めは、一人でホントに良く頑張っているから、少しは息抜きをする時間をつくってね、と
dialogue.English: At first, I told her, 'You're really doing so well on your own, you should make some time to take a break.'

dialogue.content: そういうと
dialogue.English: When I said that,

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes?

dialogue.content: それは無理だというんです
dialogue.English: she said it's impossible.

dialogue.content: 自分の母親と一緒に暮らしているんですが、そのお母さんが依存的らしくて
dialogue.English: She lives with her own mother, who seems to be very dependent,

dialogue.content: 仕事で帰りがちょっと遅くなると、ガミガミ言うし
dialogue.English: and if she gets home a little late from work, her mother nags her,

dialogue.content: そうですか・・・
dialogue.English: I see...

dialogue.content: 平日の休みの日は、病院の付き添いに付き合わせるし、
dialogue.English: and on her days off during the week, she has to accompany her to the hospital,

dialogue.content: 全く一人になる時間をもないんだそうなんです。
dialogue.English: She says she has absolutely no time to herself.

dialogue.content: そもそも、旦那さんとの別居も
dialogue.English: In the first place, her separation from her husband...

dialogue.content: お母さんと合わなくて、気を遣うかららしいんです。
dialogue.English: was apparently because he couldn't get along with her mother and found it stressful.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですか・・・
dialogue.English: I see, so that’s how it was…

dialogue.content: 親を捨てろとも言えないし
dialogue.English: I can't tell her to abandon her parent,

dialogue.content: 確かに・・・
dialogue.English: True...

dialogue.content: 疲弊している姿を見るのはとても切ないです。
dialogue.English: It's heartbreaking to see her so worn out.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。後輩の方はすっかりストレスが溜まってしまっているようですね・・・
dialogue.English: I understand. It sounds like your junior colleague is completely overwhelmed with stress…

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: でも、あなたがトイレで声をかけてあげたので、その溜まっているもののうちのわずかでもあなたに聞いてもらえたことは、その方にとっては大きかったような気がしますけど・・・
dialogue.English: But because you reached out to her in the restroom, I imagine that having you listen to even a small part of what’s been building up meant a lot to her…

dialogue.content: そうですすかね?　　彼女は、反抗期の今を乗り切れば…今だけ我慢すれば・・・そう言うんですが
dialogue.English: Do you think so? She says that if she can just get through this rebellious phase—if she can just endure it for now…

dialogue.content: 私には、単なる反抗期だけの問題じゃないように感じていて
dialogue.English: To me, it doesn’t feel like this is just about a rebellious phase.

dialogue.content: あなたとしては、彼女のお話しを聞いてどう思っていらっしゃるのですか？
dialogue.English: From your perspective, what do you think after hearing her story?

dialogue.content: そうですね
dialogue.English: Well...

dialogue.content: 彼女はどう感じているか分かりませんが
dialogue.English: I don’t know how she feels about it, but

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes?

dialogue.content: 彼女がお母さんから、お母さんの都合の良い子でいるように強いられて来たのと同じことを子ども達にやって来た結果の反抗期の爆発のように思うんです。
dialogue.English: I think this rebellious outburst is the result of her doing the same thing to her children that her mother did to her—forcing them to be the 'good child' that was convenient for the parent.

dialogue.content: 評判の良い私学も
dialogue.English: Even the well-regarded private school,

dialogue.content: なるほど。それはありそうですね。
dialogue.English: I see. That seems plausible.

dialogue.content: 一人は余裕で入ったけれど、一人は初めから、相当きつかったようなんです
dialogue.English: One of them got in easily, but for the other, it seems to have been a real struggle from the start.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。
dialogue.English: I see, so that's how it was.

dialogue.content: 2人が同じ学校に行くことが、できない子のコンプレックスを深めない事だと感じて、同じ学校に入れたようですが
dialogue.English: She felt that having both of them attend the same school would prevent the one who struggles from developing a deeper complex, so she put them in the same school, but

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 結局、コンプレックスを逆なでする結果になっているようで
dialogue.English: in the end, it seems to have had the opposite effect, aggravating his complex.

dialogue.content: かもしれませんね・・・
dialogue.English: That may be the case...

dialogue.content: ご本にとっては、同じ学校の同じ学年にいると、何かと学校でも比較されますからね・・・
dialogue.English: For the child himself, being in the same grade at the same school means they'll be compared in various ways at school, too...

dialogue.content: まだまだやり直せるから
dialogue.English: There’s still time to make changes, so

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 本人がしんどいなら、転校もあるよ、と言ったのですが、全否定されました。
dialogue.English: I told her that if it’s too hard for him, transferring schools is an option, but she completely rejected that.

dialogue.content: そうですか。後輩の方はやはり同じ学校に通わせることにこだわっていらっしゃるのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see. Is your junior colleague insistent on having them attend the same school?

dialogue.content: そうですね。本人が続けたいと言っているから、学校から首になるまでは置いてもらう、と言ってました。
dialogue.English: Yes. She said that since he says he wants to continue, she'll let him stay until the school kicks him out.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね・・・
dialogue.English: I see...

dialogue.content: ここまでのところを少し整理させていただいてもいいですか？
dialogue.English: Would it be alright if I summarized what we've discussed so far?

dialogue.content: お願いします。
dialogue.English: Please do.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 職場の後輩が最近元気がなくなっているので心配で様子を聞いてみたら次のことを話してくれた。
dialogue.English: You were worried about a junior colleague at work who's been down lately, and when you asked her about it, she told you the following.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 双子のお子さんがいて、二人とも地域の評判の私学に入学できた。
dialogue.English: She has twin sons, and both were able to get into a well-regarded local private school.

dialogue.content: 一人は余裕で入ったが、実はもう一人の子はなんとかようやく入れたという状況だった。
dialogue.English: One was admitted easily, but the other barely made it in.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ようやく入れた方の子が、最近反抗期で、母親に当たってくるのが辛い。
dialogue.English: The son who just managed to get in is going through a rebellious phase and is lashing out at his mother, which is painful for her.

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: そもそもこの子たちは本当に苦労してようやく生まれてきた子たちだった。
dialogue.English: These children were born after a great deal of hardship.

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: それで、自分としても二人の塾の送り迎えもし、精一杯育ててきた。
dialogue.English: And so, she has done her best to raise them, including driving them to and from cram school.

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 一方で、実は実母が同居しているが、その実母さんが後輩の帰りが遅い不平を言ったり、病院に付き添ったりしなければならない。
dialogue.English: Meanwhile, she lives with her own mother, who complains if she comes home late, and she has to accompany her to the hospital.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 夫さんは、この実母さんとの折り合いが悪くて、結果今は別居になってい待っている。
dialogue.English: Her husband doesn’t get along with her mother, and as a result they are now separated.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: それで、家庭の難しいことはみんな彼女の肩にかかってきてしまっている。
dialogue.English: So, all the difficult family matters have fallen on her shoulders.

dialogue.content: そうですね
dialogue.English: That’s right.

dialogue.content: このことに関して、あなたは、特にようやく私学に入った方のお子さんついては、無理せずに転校も考えることをお勧めした見たが、彼女は受け入れられなかった。
dialogue.English: Regarding this, you suggested she consider having the son who struggled to get in transfer to another school to ease the pressure, but she wouldn't accept that.

dialogue.content: その子としても、首になるまでこの学校にいると言っているとのこと。
dialogue.English: And the son himself has apparently said he'll stay at that school until he's kicked out.

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ただ
dialogue.English: However,

dialogue.content: あなたとしては、彼女はもともといい子を演じてきて、そのまま母親をやっているのでこうなってしまっていると見ていらっしゃる。
dialogue.English: From your perspective, she has long played the role of the “good child,” and has continued that pattern as a mother, which you believe has led to the current situation.

dialogue.content: 首になるまで、は、彼女の言葉なんです。
dialogue.English: “Until he gets expelled” were her words.

dialogue.content: という理解なのですが、どこか違う所があるでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Is my understanding correct, or is there anything you'd like to add or change?

dialogue.content: 「首になるまで」は後輩さんの言葉ということ了解いたしました。
dialogue.English: I understand now. The phrase 'until he's kicked out' came from your colleague.

dialogue.content: 自分の可愛い子供なのに、置いてもらう、という表現が何だか、有名私学に捉われているような気がして
dialogue.English: Even though it's her own precious child, the expression she used, 'let him stay,' makes me feel like she's fixated on the prestigious private school.

dialogue.content: たしかにそれはありそうですね。
dialogue.English: That does seem plausible.

dialogue.content: できの良い子、評価の高い子になるように関わって来たのではないかな、と思ってしまいました。
dialogue.English: It made me wonder if she's been raising them to be high-achieving, highly-regarded children.

dialogue.content: 自分がお母さんからされたように
dialogue.English: Just as her own mother did to her.

dialogue.content: 彼女は
dialogue.English: She...

dialogue.content: 国立大学を出ているんです。
dialogue.English: graduated from a national university.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 旦那さんは高校卒なんです。
dialogue.English: Her husband is a high school graduate.

dialogue.content: なるほど、そうなんですね・・・
dialogue.English: I see, so that's the situation...

dialogue.content: お母さんの中では、彼女に不釣り合いで、折り合いが悪くなったのではないかと思います。
dialogue.English: I think in her mother's eyes, her husband wasn't a good match for her, and that's why they didn't get along.

dialogue.content: かもしれませんね。
dialogue.English: That could be.

dialogue.content: 親子って、知らず知らずに連鎖するんですね。
dialogue.English: The parent-child dynamic really does get passed down without us realizing it, doesn't it?

dialogue.content: ですね。
dialogue.English: It does.

dialogue.content: 私はこれから、どんな風に接したらいいでしようか?
dialogue.English: How should I interact with her from now on?

dialogue.content: あなたなりのお考えはどんなですか？
dialogue.English: What are your own thoughts on that?

dialogue.content: あれこれアドバイスをしても、今は聴いて考えてくれる余裕もなさそうだし、
dialogue.English: Even if I give her all sorts of advice, she doesn’t seem to have the capacity to listen and think about it right now,

dialogue.content: はい　そうみたいですね。
dialogue.English: Yes, that seems to be the case.

dialogue.content: ちょっと距離を置いて見守るしかないかな、と思うのですが
dialogue.English: I feel like maybe the only thing I can do is keep a little distance and watch over her, but...

dialogue.content: そんな事してて、自殺でもしちゃったら、と思うと、どうしていいか迷います。
dialogue.English: when I think about what would happen if she were to do something like commit suicide while I'm doing that, I get lost and don't know what to do.

dialogue.content: たしかにそこは、悩みますね・・
dialogue.English: That is certainly a difficult point to navigate...

dialogue.content: どうでしょうか、しばし後輩の方の聞き役に徹してあげるというのは、いかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: What do you think about dedicating yourself to being a listener for your colleague for a while?

dialogue.content: そうですね。
dialogue.English: That makes sense.

dialogue.content: でも、以前のように、声をかけてくれないから・・・
dialogue.English: But she doesn’t reach out to me like she used to…

dialogue.content: こちらから、声はかけても良いんでしょうか?
dialogue.English: Is it okay for me to reach out to her?

dialogue.content: それもお節介にも思えます。
dialogue.English: I feel like that might be meddling.

dialogue.content: 前回トイレでお声がけしたように、機会をみつけて、さりげなく声をかけてお話を聞いてあげるのはいかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: As you did last time in the restroom, perhaps you could find opportunities to casually check in and listen to her.

dialogue.content: そうですね。タイミングがあったら、さりげなく声をかけて、話したいようなら聴く、というスタンスですね。
dialogue.English: Right. If the timing is right, I’ll casually reach out, and if she seems to want to talk, I’ll listen—that's the stance.

dialogue.content: そんな風にやってみます。
dialogue.English: I'll try doing it that way.

dialogue.content: もし、その方が孤立して悩んでいらっしゃるなら、きっと、誰かに話しを聞いてもらいたいと思っていると思いますよ。
dialogue.English: If she is feeling isolated and struggling, I'm sure she wants someone to listen to her.

dialogue.content: そうですね。
dialogue.English: You're right.

dialogue.content: あなたのような先輩がいるなんて、その後輩さんはラッキーですよ。
dialogue.English: Your colleague is lucky to have a senior like you.

dialogue.content: そうですかね。
dialogue.English: Do you think so?

dialogue.content: 私は今日お話しを聞いていて断然、そう思いましたよ。
dialogue.English: Listening to you today, I absolutely think so.

dialogue.content: 何もしてあげれずに、おろおろしているだけなんですが
dialogue.English: I just feel flustered, unable to do anything for her.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 話を聞いてもらえるだけでも、大きいですよ。
dialogue.English: Just having someone listen can make a huge difference.

dialogue.content: 少しでも良い聞き役になれるように頑張ってみます。
dialogue.English: I'll do my best to be as good a listener as I can be.

dialogue.content: そうして、あなたはあなたなりの見解をお持ちになっているので、その点も大きなことだと思いますよ。
dialogue.English: And the fact that you have your own perspective on the situation is also a very significant thing.

dialogue.content: あれこれ詮索して、良いんでしょうかね?
dialogue.English: Is it really okay for me to probe into various things like this?

dialogue.content: 詮索というより、相手の方のために一緒に考えて差し上げているということだと思いますよ。
dialogue.English: I think it's less about probing and more about thinking things through together for her sake.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: この件は、なかなか複雑な要素がありそうなので、気になることが出てきたら、是非またご相談にいらしていただけたらと思います。
dialogue.English: This matter seems to have many complex elements, so if anything else comes up that concerns you, please feel free to come back and talk about it.

dialogue.content: よろしければご一緒に考えさせていただきます。
dialogue.English: If you’d like, I would be happy to think it through with you.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。彼女のこれからに、少しでも力になれればと思います。
dialogue.English: Thank you. I hope I can be of some help to her going forward.

dialogue.content: 宜しくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: I appreciate your support.

dialogue.content: そこが素敵な先輩さんですよ。
dialogue.English: That’s what makes you a wonderful senior colleague.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。少し気持ちが楽になりました。
dialogue.English: Thank you. I feel a bit more at ease now.

dialogue.content: よかったです。では今日はこの辺で一旦失礼させていただいてもよろしいですか？
dialogue.English: I'm glad to hear that. Would it be alright if we conclude our session for today?

dialogue.content: はい、大丈夫です。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Yes, that’s fine. Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: こちらこそ、今日はご相談に来てくださりありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you for coming in to talk with me today.

dialogue.content: では、失礼させていただきます。
dialogue.English: Well then, goodbye for now.

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you.
